published_source: Printed Table 2, column (1) (ITT) of the published article (papers/mnsc/mnsc.2021.02026.pdf), read Nov 4 2026; equals the authors' full-data code output (the shipped log) to the printed decimals; the authors' code re-run on the shipped 10 percent random seller sample gives 0.002466 (0.017203), N 423706, which differs because of the subsample. Earlier: PanelMainAnalysis.R line 80 (ITT); full-data log logPanelMainAnalysis_Lines1_105.txt. Abstract: access to SH increases revenues by 3.6%.
replication_status: failed (random_subsample; same-sign-within-10-percent rule not met: the package ships a 10 percent random seller sample, so the printed full-data value is not reproducible from the shipped data; printed Table 2, column (1) (ITT) 0.035 (0.005), N 4,237,106; the authors' full-data log 0.03482 (0.005467), N 4237106, equals it to the printed decimals; the authors' code re-run on the shipped sample gives 0.002466 (0.017203), N 423706, same sign, a gap of 93 percent of the printed value, within 1.96 subsample SEs (z = -1.88); verified against the article Nov 4 2026)
notes: gvar = gweek = first panel week with SHaccess = 1 (NA for the Aug 8 never-treated-in-window group), computed on the full balanced seller-week panel before any sample restriction, so cohorts stay correct in the unbalanced Price/Feedback samples (deriving the adoption week from the first observed treated row in the Price>0 sample produced 13 spurious cohorts). D = 1[week >= gweek] equals the authors' SHaccess row by row in every regression sample. Headline ITT. Appendix A5.5 (full data) reports for this spec: Callaway-Sant'Anna simple ATT 0.03671 (0.00703), Sun-Abraham 0.03699 (0.00713), Roth-Sant'Anna efficient 0.07051 (0.00644) via the staggered package, vs TWFE 0.03482. Bar-Gill, Brynjolfsson and Hak (2024), eBay Seller Hub (SH) randomized staggered rollout. Seller x week panel, 23 Saturday week-ending dates 2016-03-05..2016-08-06. Treatment SHaccess = 1[WeekEndingDate >= TreatmentDate], absorbing; 6 in-window access cohorts (May 12, May 19, Jun 6, Jun 13, Jun 21, Jul 26 2016 = weeks 11, 12, 15, 16, 17, 22) plus the Aug 8 group, whose access date falls after the last panel week and is therefore never treated in-window (31.3% of sellers). No always-treated units, no switch-offs. Seller FE + week FE, no controls, no weights, SE clustered by seller (authors: lfe::felm, exactDOF=T). DATA: the package ships only a 10% random seller sample (18,422 of 184,222 sellers; 423,706 seller-weeks); the full files need eBay legal approval (README). Prepared panel built by _work/mnsc.2021.02026/build_panel.R, which mirrors PanelMainAnalysis.R lines 15-66; log outcomes precomputed (logSales = log(GMV+1), etc.). published_coef/published_se are the FULL-DATA values from the package log logPanelMainAnalysis_Lines*.txt (stargazer output identical to the published table columns); the article PDF is not in the project so they are unverified against the printed tables. On the 10% sample fixest reproduces the authors' felm line exactly (coefficients identical to 8+ digits, SE identical to 4 digits); the subsample estimate differs from the full-data value by sampling error (SEs about 3.2x larger).
